action.description: Mirrors audit.Action. Subset applicable to operator mutations.

actor.description: Principal who made the change. Format: '<subsystem>:<principal>'.

after.description: Compact snapshot of resource after change. null on delete.

before.description: Compact snapshot of resource before change. null on create.

version_from.description: Content hash / semver of resource before change.

version_to.description: Content hash / semver of resource after change.

after.description: Present for add + replace. Redacted if sensitive.

before.description: Present for replace + remove. Redacted if sensitive.

path.description: JSON pointer / dotted path. Array indices rendered as 'field[n]'.

document.description: Populates the `activity` sub-object on a gateway-event-envelope when event_type="activity". Records operator-facing mutations: config save, policy reload, block/allow list update, skill approval, sink reconfiguration. Carries before/after snapshots plus a structured diff so compliance auditors can reconstruct every change without scraping CLI output.
document.title: DefenseClaw Activity Event Payload (v7)

document.description: Row persisted in audit_events (SQLite) and forwarded to Splunk/HTTP sinks. v7 adds provenance (SchemaVersion=7) + three-tier agent identity. Consumers MUST treat every field marked optional as nullable — not every action emits every field.

action.description: Curated action — see internal/audit/actions.go (Go) and cli/defenseclaw/audit_actions.py (Python). Extending this enum is a minor schema bump. The `codex.notify.<sanitized-type>` family is dynamic: the gateway derives the suffix from the codex notify payload after sanitization ([a-z0-9._-]{1,64}). Validators MUST accept either the static enum OR the prefixed pattern.

oneOf.description: Dynamic codex notify suffix family. Suffix is derived from the inbound payload's `type` field via sanitizeNotifyType.

agent_id.description: Stable agent identity across process restarts.

agent_instance_id.description: Per-session agent identity — rotates on new session.

binary_version.description: Semver of the DefenseClaw binary that produced the event.

connector.description: Multi-connector identity: the hook connector that produced this event (codex, claudecode, antigravity, ...). Recovered from request context; null for proxy / non-connector events.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON serialization of the emitting config / policy at emit time. Optional; present when the event describes a configurable surface.

details.description: Redacted legacy free-form detail blob. Treat as opaque. Connector-hook rows keep a transitional details_json= token here for older parsers; new consumers should prefer structured.

enforced.description: True when the guardrail decision was actually enforced (blocked), as opposed to an observe-mode would-block. Null/absent for non-enforcement events.

generation.description: Monotonic counter incremented on every Save of the governing config/policy. Optional.

parent_span_id.description: W3C trace-context parent span id, propagated via the traceparent header by the OTel SDK. Optional — present when the event was emitted inside an active span with a parent.

rule_pack_dir.description: Effective rule-pack directory the verdict was evaluated against (per-connector override or global). Null when no rule pack applies.

schema_version.description: Audit row format version. v7 = provenance + three-tier agent identity. Downstream MUST reject unrecognized versions.

sidecar_instance_id.description: Per-process sidecar identity — rotates on every defenseclaw gateway start.

step_idx.description: 1-indexed per-turn counter within a session_id. A turn is one prompt-response cycle; all hook events emitted during the same turn share one step_idx. Null/absent when the event is not turn-anchored.

structured.description: Optional first-class machine-readable payload stored in audit_events.structured_json and forwarded to audit sinks. Connector-hook rows use hook-audit-envelope.json (schema=defenseclaw.hook.v1).

target.description: Target of the action (skill id, mcp server id, policy id, etc). Nullable — lifecycle events like 'init' and 'ready' have no target.

trace_flags.description: W3C trace-context trace-flags (e.g. '01' sampled), propagated via the traceparent header. Optional.

raw_path.description: populated only when privacy.disable_redaction=true AND ai_discovery.store_raw_local_paths=true

raw_paths.description: populated only when privacy.disable_redaction=true AND ai_discovery.store_raw_local_paths=true

evaluation_id.description: Optional join key linking this error to the evaluation that produced the broken event (matches ScanPayload.evaluation_id / VerdictPayload.evaluation_id).

rule_id.description: Optional rule identifier this error is attributable to (schema-gate violations on finding events, verdict-failure errors).

HookDecisionPayload.description: The final action delivered to a hook connector. action may differ from raw_action when observe mode or connector capability downgrades a guardrail block; this is the durable source for recovery-path analysis.

evaluation_id.description: Optional join key linking this verdict to its per-finding scan_findings rows / EventScanFinding fan-out.

rule_ids.description: Top detection rule identifiers that drove this verdict (capped at 8). Quick SIEM-pivot key.

document.description: One JSONL line emitted by the DefenseClaw gateway sidecar to gateway.jsonl / stderr / HTTP sinks. The envelope carries correlation + provenance; exactly one of the type-specific payload sub-objects is populated and selected by `event_type`. `hook_decision` records the final connector-facing action after enforcement-mode/capability mapping, distinct from the underlying guardrail verdict.

deployment_mode.description: Sidecar deployment mode. Populated from config deployment_mode when set.

discovery_source.description: How the monitored agent or tool was discovered. Populated from config discovery_source when set.

environment.description: Deployment environment. Populated from config environment when set.

tenant_id.description: Logical tenancy boundary for hosted/SaaS deployments. Populated from config tenant_id when set.

workspace_id.description: Sub-tenant workspace, organization, or team scope. Populated from config workspace_id when set.

document.description: Machine-readable payload stored on audit_events.structured_json for connector hook outcomes. The legacy audit details string may also carry this same object as details_json during migration.

action.description: Normalized action returned to the connector when present.

body_bytes.description: Inbound request body size for malformed or rejected hook submissions.

connector.description: DefenseClaw connector/profile name, for example codex, claudecode, cursor, geminicli, or openhands.

enforced.description: True when the decision was an enforced block (not an observe-mode would-block). Mirrors audit_events.enforced.

event.description: Connector hook event name after DefenseClaw normalization.

extra.description: Connector-specific string dimensions. Keys and values are log-injection sanitized before emission.

mode.description: Connector enforcement mode, commonly action or observe.

raw_action.description: Raw hook action before mode downgrades such as observe-mode allow.

raw_payload.description: Optional redacted raw hook payload retained only when the caller explicitly enables raw capture.

reason.description: Redacted human-readable reason for the hook decision.

result.description: Outcome of the hook collector invocation.

rule_pack_dir.description: Effective rule-pack directory the verdict used. Mirrors audit_events.rule_pack_dir.

schema.description: Stable hook envelope schema identifier. Bump only for incompatible wire changes.

step_idx.description: 1-indexed per-turn counter within a session. Mirrors audit_events.step_idx so the structured_json sink and the SQLite column agree.

would_block.description: True when the hook verdict represents a block posture, including observe mode downgrades.

document.description: A single outbound network call observed by the agent runtime, with policy decision fields stored as first-class structured data.

agent_execution_id.description: One execution attempt within the stable lifecycle.

agent_lifecycle_id.description: Stable lifecycle identifier retained across resumes.

blocked.description: true when the call was actively prevented by policy.

connector.description: Hook or proxy connector that observed the call.

decision_code.description: Machine-readable outcome token for programmatic filtering.

details.description: Additional context such as the matched policy pattern.

http_method.description: HTTP verb (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS).

parent_agent_id.description: Direct parent agent when this event belongs to a delegated agent.

policy_outcome.description: Human-readable summary of the policy decision.

root_agent_id.description: Root agent for this multi-agent execution tree.

root_session_id.description: Root conversation/session for the multi-agent execution tree.

session_id.description: Agent session identifier. Correlates this event with tool_call/tool_result rows for the same session.

severity.description: Event severity. Defaults to HIGH for blocked calls and INFO for allowed calls.

timestamp.description: When the call was observed (RFC3339). Defaults to the ingestion time when omitted.

tool_id.description: Tool call identifier that initiated the network action.

url.description: Full destination URL. Stored at most 512 characters.

user_id.description: User principal associated with the agent lifecycle.

document.description: Resource attributes attached to all OTLP exports (logs, traces, metrics). Set once at sidecar startup.

defenseclaw.claw.home_dir.description: Resolved home directory of the active claw framework. Path layout is connector-specific: openclaw uses ~/.openclaw, zeptoclaw uses ~/.zeptoclaw, claudecode uses ~/.claude (or $CLAUDE_HOME), codex uses ~/.codex, hermes uses ~/.hermes, cursor uses ~/.cursor, windsurf uses ~/.codeium/windsurf, geminicli uses ~/.gemini, copilot uses ~/.copilot while workspace assets may live under .github/, openhands uses workspace .openhands plus ~/.openhands for MCP, opencode uses ~/.config/opencode, and omnigent uses $OMNIGENT_CONFIG_HOME when set or ~/.omnigent otherwise.

defenseclaw.claw.mode.description: Active agent framework connector. Matches Connector.Name() in internal/gateway/connector. Empty string is permitted while no connector has been picked yet (fresh install before `defenseclaw setup connector`). The 'multi' sentinel is emitted when a single gateway process serves more than one connector simultaneously; in that case this process-level attribute does not name an individual connector and consumers must read the per-event `connector` metric label / `defenseclaw.connector.source` span attribute for the true connector. Legacy value 'nemoclaw' was never emitted by a released gateway and has been dropped from the enum.

defenseclaw.device.id.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 fingerprint of the DefenseClaw Ed25519 device public key. This is DefenseClaw pairing identity, not a host hardware UUID or generic endpoint identifier.

defenseclaw.instance.id.description: UUID generated at sidecar startup. Unique per process lifetime.

deployment.environment.description: Detected runtime environment. Recommended values are 'macos', 'dgx-spark', and 'linux' for the in-tree probes; operators with bespoke deployments can override via configuration (e.g. 'prod-us-east-1', 'staging'). Downstream dashboards must treat unknown values as opaque rather than enforce an allow-list.

service.name.description: Service name attached to every OTLP export. Defaults to 'defenseclaw' but can be overridden via OTEL_SERVICE_NAME or otel.resource.attributes for fleet identification (e.g. 'defenseclaw-prod-eu-west-1'). Operators MUST keep the value short and stable — downstream Splunk APM dashboards group by this attribute.

service.namespace.description: Service namespace for grouping in Splunk APM.

defenseclaw.alert.trigger.direction.description: Whether the flagged content was in the LLM input or output.

defenseclaw.alert.trigger.tool.description: Tool name, if the alert was triggered by a tool call.

defenseclaw.guardrail.confidence.description: Confidence score from the guardrail (if available).

defenseclaw.guardrail.policy.description: Policy name or rule that triggered the alert.

document.description: OTEL LogRecord emitted on scan completion. Body contains the full structured scan result; attributes provide indexed fields for Splunk queries.

body.description: JSON-encoded scan summary as OTEL AnyValue.

stringValue.description: JSON string of the scan result body.

severityText.description: Derived from MaxSeverity: CRITICAL→ERROR, HIGH→WARN, else INFO.

timeUnixNano.description: Scan completion timestamp in nanoseconds since Unix epoch.

document.title: DefenseClaw Scan Result Event

counts.description: Severity -> count. Keys are a subset of severity_max enum.

error.description: Scanner execution error. Present only when the wrapper failed (timeout, non-zero exit).

evaluation_id.description: Optional join key linking this scan to its upstream runtime evaluation (hook handler, /api/v1/inspect/*, proxy guardrail, mid-stream, tool-call-inspect, watcher rescan). Empty for classic scanner-invocation paths.

scan_id.description: Correlation id shared by the roll-up EventScan and all child EventScanFinding events.

scanner.description: Source of the finding. Classic scanner invocations use skill|mcp|plugin|aibom|codeguard. Runtime finding emitters fanned out via EmitInspectFindings use hook-rules|inline-codeguard|ai-defense|asset-policy|tool-call-inspect|inspect-http|guardrail-llm|mid-stream|rescan.

target.description: File path | skill name | server URL | tool name | message surface. Redacted when scanner contract requires.

document.description: Populates the `scan` sub-object on a gateway-event-envelope when event_type="scan". Summarises one scanner invocation — findings are fanned out as sibling EventScanFinding events sharing the same scan_id.
document.title: DefenseClaw Scan Event Payload (v7)

confidence.description: Detector self-reported certainty in [0,1]. Omitted by binary scanners.

evaluation_id.description: Optional join key matching the parent ScanPayload.evaluation_id.

rule_id.description: Stable detection rule identifier. Preferred group-by for SIEM; never display-string.

scanner.description: Source of the finding. Classic scanner invocations use skill|mcp|plugin|aibom|codeguard. Runtime finding emitters fanned out via EmitInspectFindings use hook-rules|inline-codeguard|ai-defense|asset-policy|tool-call-inspect|inspect-http|guardrail-llm|mid-stream|rescan.

document.description: Populates the `scan_finding` sub-object on a gateway-event-envelope when event_type="scan_finding". One emission per scanner finding; downstream SIEM can alert on a single critical finding without joining against the parent EventScan summary.
document.title: DefenseClaw Scan Finding Event Payload (v7)

document.description: Canonical scanner output — what skill-scanner / mcp-scanner / plugin-scanner / aibom / codeguard serialize as the CLI `--output json` payload and what gets persisted to audit.scan_results.raw_output. v7 extends the Finding shape with rule_id + line_number for SIEM-safe grouping, and extends the envelope with the provenance quartet.

line_number.description: v7 — 1-based source line; 0 or null when not meaningful.

rule_id.description: v7 — stable detection rule identifier for SIEM group-by.

scan_id.description: v7 correlation id shared with gateway-event-envelope EventScan + child EventScanFinding events.

scanner.description: Source of the scan. Classic scanner invocations use skill|mcp|plugin|aibom|codeguard (or their *-scanner aliases). Runtime finding emitters fanned out via EmitInspectFindings use hook-rules|inline-codeguard|ai-defense|asset-policy|tool-call-inspect|inspect-http|guardrail-llm|mid-stream|rescan.
